findings.claim: The boundary_rationale carries a WEB paragraph-block fact as a layout signal 'consistent with' this row's span, and it is the only external corroboration the row offers for a closing seam that carries no frame onset and no parashah mark, in a row shipping high confidence.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale closes: 'WEB prints Isa.24.1-13 as one paragraph block (a tier-4 layout signal consistent with, but not the basis for, this row).' The WEB layout fact is true in the staged text (a paragraph opens at web:Isa.24.1 and the next opens at web:Isa.24.14, with none between), but WEB paragraphing is tier-4 and is barred as a boundary ground whether as driver or as corroboration. At the Isa.24.13|Isa.24.14 seam nothing else external stands: the parashah inventory's nearest marks are PE at MT 23:18 and SAMEKH at MT 24:15 (single-witness), with no mark at the seam; the chapter census the row itself reports re-verifies against the staged device inventory (0 verse-initial massa headers, 0 hoy onsets, 0 koh-amar sites, 0 postpositive neum signatures, 0 amar-or-vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacencies in this chapter), and the sole day-formula site in the chapter is MT 24:21, not the seam; and both sides of the seam are third person with no addressee on either side, כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת (oshb:Isa.24.13, byte tier) against הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ (oshb:Isa.24.14, byte tier), so the shift there is of subject only.
findings.proposed_change: Strike the WEB paragraph-block sentence from boundary_rationale and re-derive confidence from what remains at the Isa.24.13|Isa.24.14 seam (a subject shift inside continuous third-person narration, no frame onset, no mark).

findings.claim: The divine-utterance formula note attaches a skeleton-tier twin and a 4-verse sweep digit to the six-word run it splices, but that run is unique to its own verse at every tier; the digit belongs to a short formula the row never splices.
findings.grounds: device_notes reads '(oshb:Isa.24.3, byte tier; skeleton tier only against its nearest twin at oshb:Isa.22.25, with the same short formula recurring at two further sites elsewhere in the book - sweep: 4 verses skeleton tier)' for the splice כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.24.3, byte tier). Re-swept, that exact run stands at 1 verse at byte tier, 1 at accent_stripped and 1 at skeleton - oshb:Isa.24.3 alone - so it has no skeleton-tier twin at oshb:Isa.22.25 and no recurrence anywhere. The 4-verse digit belongs to a different, never-spliced count object, the short formula כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.22.25, byte tier): its skeleton sweeps to 4 verses book-wide (Isa.1.2, Isa.22.25, Isa.24.3, Isa.25.8), one of which, oshb:Isa.25.8, is the closing clause of a sibling row of this same part rather than a site 'elsewhere in the book' in any neutral sense.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the parenthetical so the tier and the digit attach to the object actually swept: splice the short formula from oshb:Isa.22.25, state that the six-word run at oshb:Isa.24.3 is unique to its own verse at every tier, and cite the 4-verse skeleton digit against the short formula with its sites named.

findings.claim: A byte-true anaphoric dependency straddles this row's own closing seam and is disclosed only by the following row, never here.
findings.grounds: The bare pronoun opening the next verse, הֵ֛מָּה (oshb:Isa.24.14, byte tier), takes its referent from the gleaning image closing this row's final verse, כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת (oshb:Isa.24.13, byte tier). Under the campaign's cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed; this row's prose never mentions it, while the immediately following row discloses it in its own device_notes with the same two splices.
findings.proposed_change: Add the anaphora to this row's device_notes as a disclosed cross-seam dependency, with the byte-tier splices at oshb:Isa.24.13 and oshb:Isa.24.14, and state what warrant survives it.

findings.claim: The sentence device_notes names as 'the warrant that survives' the cross-seam anaphora asserts that the two verses are narrated wholly in the third person with no addressee change inside them, which the row's own closing verse contradicts in its bytes.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'the warrant that survives it is that the group so identified is nonetheless narrated wholly in the third person through Isa.24.15, with no addressee or scene change of its own inside the two verses.' The row's closing verse turns on a plural imperative, כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.24.15, byte tier), rendered “Therefore glorify Yahweh in the east” (web:Isa.24.15) - direct address to an audience, against the third-person narration of יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ (oshb:Isa.24.14, byte tier), “These shall lift up their voice. They will shout for the majesty of Yahweh.” (web:Isa.24.14). The row's own boundary_rationale states the same fact against itself ('the summons continues as an imperative call') and observed_substrate_signals carries hymn.praise_summons_imperative, so the two fields contradict each other and the one carrying the row's opening seam is the byte-false one. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims under the tier-disclosure standard, and both witnesses read an imperative here.
findings.proposed_change: Repair the surviving-warrant sentence so it rests on what the bytes carry - one sung praise-reaction with a single referent group across the couplet, with the third-person-to-imperative turn inside it disclosed rather than denied; because this is the warrant that carries the row's own opening seam, re-open strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence with it. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: Two of this row's four observed_substrate_signals are parashah.* keys, which this audit's method bars but the owner-ratified oss field contract in the governing book strategy expressly permits - recorded as a rule conflict for adjudication, not as an assertion that the row is wrong.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries parashah.petuchah_single_witness and parashah.setumah_single_witness beside oracle_frame.bayom_hahu_onset and divine_title.yhwh_tsevaot. The audit method bars parashah.* in that field; the owner-ratified field contract lists parashah.* among the permitted dotted signal classes. Nothing else in the row is defective: the mark claims re-verify against the parashah inventory as SAMEKH at MT 24:20 and PE at MT 24:23 (single-witness, types not conflated), device_notes labels both 'tier-3, non-driving', and both edges are tier-1 and byte-verified - וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier), the chapter's only day-formula site at any tier, and מָלַ֞ךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת (oshb:Isa.24.23, byte tier) - with the row's claim that no second day-formula onset interrupts Isa.24.21-23 re-swept and confirmed.

findings.claim: The closing-edge warrant rests on the second-person register running through this row's final verse, but that verse's own second colon is third person and is nowhere disclosed, while the row ships at high confidence with the frontier flag unset in a region the governing strategy registers as expected-low-confidence.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'The second-person address to Yahweh continues through Isa.25.5, closing on a second-person verb, תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier)'. That form stands at the athnach, not at the verse end; the row's final verse closes זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier), rendered “the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low” (web:Isa.25.5) - third person, so the register the warrant relies on has already lapsed inside the row's own last verse, and the intra-verse turn is disclosed nowhere in the row. The edge itself survives on grounds standing in the next verse's bytes, וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier), “In this mountain, Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast” (web:Isa.25.6), plus PE at MT 25:5 (single-witness, tier-3, non-driving). The owner-ruled book strategy registers the 24-27 cycle's song insets, 25:1-5 among them, as an expected low-confidence region for exactly this voice alternation, yet confidence is high and frontier_flag_considered is false.
findings.proposed_change: Disclose the third-person close of Isa.25.5 in device_notes with its byte-tier splice, re-state the closing warrant as resting on Isa.25.6's own explicit third-person divine subject plus the PE bracket, and re-derive confidence and the frontier flag against the registered low-confidence region. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: An in-span paseq seg is left undisclosed while sibling rows of this same part disclose theirs in the same field.
findings.grounds: The paseq inventory records 1 seg at MT 25:7 (single-witness, count-only), inside this row's own span Isa.25.6-Isa.25.8. device_notes discloses the PE marks at MT 25:5 and MT 25:8 and the in-span recurrence band, but says nothing of the paseq, whereas two other rows of this part disclose their in-span paseq explicitly ('MT 24:3 also carries 2 paseq segs (single-witness, count-only)'), so the omission is a symmetry gap rather than a house style. Everything else in the row re-verifies: בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier) sweeps to 2 verses at byte tier (Isa.25.6, Isa.25.7) and 3 at accent_stripped (adding Isa.25.10), with 0 hits at any tier in Isa.25.8 and Isa.25.9, exactly as the row states.
findings.proposed_change: Add the count-only paseq disclosure for MT 25:7 (single-witness) to device_notes; no other field changes.

findings.claim: The closing-edge driver is stated as a turn from the song's second-person address of Yahweh to a third-person maxim, but the bytes run the other way: the row's last two verses are third-person description and second-person address to Yahweh resumes immediately past the seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'The row's closing edge is driven by a fresh gnomic subject opening Isa.26.7, אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.26.7, byte tier), turning from the song's own second-person address of Yahweh to a third-person maxim about the righteous', and strongest_rejected_alternative repeats the same ground. In the bytes the row's own last two verses are third-person description of God's act - כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם ... יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ (oshb:Isa.26.5, byte tier) and תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל (oshb:Isa.26.6, byte tier) - while second-person address to Yahweh stands only once inside the whole span, תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ (oshb:Isa.26.3, byte tier). Past the seam the second-person register is explicit and sustained: יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס (oshb:Isa.26.7, byte tier), rendered “You who are upright make the path of the righteous level.” (web:Isa.26.7), then אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ (oshb:Isa.26.8, byte tier), “Yes, in the way of your judgments, Yahweh, we have waited for you.” (web:Isa.26.8). The stated shift is therefore false in its direction on both sides of the seam; what survives in the bytes is only the nominal gnomic register of Isa.26.7's first colon.
findings.proposed_change: Re-argue the closing edge from what the bytes carry - the nominal gnomic colon opening Isa.26.7 against the third-person description closing Isa.26.5-26.6 - and drop the person-shift characterisation from both boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative, re-deriving confidence with it. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: WEB quotation punctuation, dressed with a sweep-style digit, is offered as corroboration of the closing edge in both boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative - and with the person-shift warrant removed it is the only external support the edge has left.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'WEB's own quotation punctuation opens at “We have a strong city” (web:Isa.26.1) and closes at “The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor and the steps of the needy.” (web:Isa.26.6), with 0 further quotation-punctuation instances resuming before Isa.27.2's separate vineyard-song frame; this is disclosed here as a tier-4, non-driving corroboration of the same edge, not its warrant'; strongest_rejected_alternative restates it as what 'corroborates the same edge without driving it'. The WEB fact re-verifies exactly (one double quotation mark in web:Isa.26.1, one in web:Isa.26.6, and 0 in web:Isa.26.7 through web:Isa.27.1), but translation punctuation is tier-4 and is barred as a boundary ground as driver and as corroboration alike, and carrying it with a digit gives tier-4 metadata the outward form of a sweep. The parashah layer marks nothing at the Isa.26.6|Isa.26.7 seam - its nearest mark is SAMEKH at MT 26:10 (single-witness) - and absence there is never counterevidence, so once the person-shift ground of the first finding is removed the tier-4 punctuation stands alone beside the gnomic-register observation, in a row shipping high confidence with frontier_flag_considered false in the expected-low-confidence song-inset region the owner-ruled strategy registers for 26:1-6.
findings.proposed_change: Strike the quotation-punctuation sentence from boundary_rationale and its restatement from strongest_rejected_alternative, and re-derive confidence and the frontier flag from the byte-grounded remainder.

findings.claim: An in-span paseq seg is left undisclosed while sibling rows of this same part disclose theirs.
findings.grounds: The paseq inventory records 1 seg at MT 26:3 (single-witness, count-only), inside this row's own span Isa.26.1-Isa.26.6. device_notes discloses the SAMEKH before the span and the absence of parashah marks inside it, but not the paseq; another row of this part discloses its in-span paseq in the same field. The row's other disclosure digits do re-verify: the short Yah form stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (Isa.12.2, Isa.26.4, Isa.38.11) per the staged device inventory, and the closing-cadence run עַד עָפָֽר (oshb:Isa.26.5, byte tier) is byte-identical at exactly one further site book-wide, oshb:Isa.25.12 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), as claimed.
findings.proposed_change: Add the count-only paseq disclosure for MT 26:3 (single-witness) to device_notes.

findings.claim: The cross-seam visitation catchword is claimed to agree 'at the consonantal skeleton' with an 18-verse digit, but the two forms share no skeleton at all, the digit belongs to the bare three-consonant substring, and the row on the other side of the same seam states the relation correctly.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier) and יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) agree only at the consonantal skeleton, which stands at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses) - not byte-identical to each other'. Re-swept, לִפְקֹ֛ד stands at skeleton tier in exactly 1 verse book-wide (Isa.26.21) and יִפְקֹ֣ד at skeleton tier in 5 (Isa.23.17, Isa.24.21, Isa.24.22, Isa.27.1, Isa.27.3): the two hit sets are disjoint, so there is no shared skeleton to agree at. The 18-verse digit is the count for the bare three-consonant substring of the root, a different count object. The following row, arguing the same seam-crossing device at the same seam, states it correctly ('links only at the shared three-consonant root, not at byte tier or at the whole-token skeleton'), so the seam-pair describes one device incompatibly.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the sentence to the bytes: the two forms are distinct attested spellings agreeing only at the three-consonant root, with the 18-verse digit named as a contiguous consonantal substring count rather than a skeleton count.

findings.claim: An 18-verse digit taken from a contiguous consonantal substring sweep is cited as a book-wide count 'on the root', which under-counts the root's attested spellings.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'לִפְקֹ֛ד and יִפְקֹ֣ד are two distinct attested spellings of that root (sweep: 18 verses book-wide on the root)'. The relation itself re-verifies exactly as stated - the two forms share no byte and no whole-token skeleton - and 18 verses is the correct count for the contiguous consonantal substring; it is not a root count, since the same root stands at oshb:Isa.10.28 in the spelling יַפְקִ֥יד (byte tier), rendered “At Michmash he stores his baggage.” (web:Isa.10.28), which a contiguous-substring sweep of the three consonants does not reach. Every other digit and mark claim in this row re-verifies: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) stands at exactly 3 verses at byte tier book-wide, יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) at exactly 2 (Isa.27.1, Isa.27.3), and the parashah inventory gives SAMEKH at MT 26:21, MT 27:1 and MT 27:6 as the row claims.
findings.proposed_change: Name the swept object as the contiguous consonantal substring rather than the root, or cite the root by its attested spellings.
